sites.ownership: Reveal cancellation borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Tab-to-tree synchronization needs one cleanup path that can disconnect reveal signals and sources before root or selection changes continue.

sites.ownership: Expanded-row restore borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Refresh and show-hidden toggles need to restore expansion state opportunistically while the lazy model repopulates.

sites.ownership: Reveal synchronization borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Selected-tab changes need one coordinated place to start or cancel reveal and clear selection when files are outside the active root.

sites.ownership: Reveal startup mutates shared project state.
sites.justification: Starting reveal must cancel any previous reveal, install the new generation, and wire temporary model-change sources against the active project tree.

sites.ownership: Reveal cleanup mutates shared project state.
sites.justification: Every reveal exit path must share cleanup so model signal handlers and GLib sources cannot outlive their generation.

sites.ownership: Deferred reveal cleanup borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Selection and model changes can re-enter reveal cleanup while project state is already borrowed, so the fallback schedules cleanup for the next main-loop turn instead of panicking.

sites.ownership: Reveal selection cleanup borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Reveal cancellation clones the GTK selection handle before clearing it so selection notifications cannot re-enter while the project state borrow is still active.

sites.ownership: Reveal model-change wiring borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: The temporary items-changed handler is owned by the pending reveal generation and must be registered and disconnected with the shared reveal state.

sites.ownership: Reveal watchdog scheduling mutates shared project state.
sites.justification: Unreachable targets need bounded cleanup through the same pending reveal generation and source tracking as normal reveal work.

sites.ownership: Reveal step scheduling mutates shared project state.
sites.justification: Model-change bursts must coalesce into one idle reveal step while preserving generation checks and queued source ownership.

sites.ownership: Reveal step execution borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: The reveal state machine needs the active tree model, selection, chain index, and generation to expand directories or select the final target safely.

sites.ownership: Reveal step planning borrows shared project state.
sites.justification: Planning a reveal step reads the pending generation and visible tree model without mutating GTK state, so expansion can happen after borrows are dropped.

sites.ownership: Reveal chain advancement mutates shared project state.
sites.justification: Lazy directory reveal advances one path component at a time and must ignore stale generation callbacks.

sites.ownership: Reveal test helper reads shared project state.
sites.justification: GTK regression tests need to assert that watchdog and cancellation paths clear pending reveal state without exposing this as runtime API.

sites.ownership: Reveal test helper starts reveal from shared project state.
sites.justification: GTK regression tests need direct reveal entry points for back-to-back and unreachable-target coverage without depending on workspace tab timing.
